knowledge_points.name: Social psychology
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Social psychology is a broad field devoted to studying the way that people relate to others.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究人们如何与他人相处的学科

knowledge_points.name: Social cognition
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This field applies many of the concepts you learned about in the field of cognition, such as memory and biases, to help explain how people think about themselves and others.
knowledge_points.plain: 用认知规律解释人如何思考他人

knowledge_points.name: Social influence theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another key concept is social influence theory, the idea that how people feel and act is affected by the other people around them.
knowledge_points.plain: 周围人影响人的感受与行为

knowledge_points.name: Attribution theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Attribution theory tries to explain how people determine the cause of what they observe.
knowledge_points.plain: 解释人如何判断行为原因

knowledge_points.name: Dispositional attribution
knowledge_points.definition_quote: For instance, if your friend Charley told you he got a perfect score on his math test, you might find yourself thinking that Charley is very good at math. In that case, you have made a dispositional attribution or person attribution.
knowledge_points.plain: 把行为归因于个人特质

knowledge_points.name: Situation attribution
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Alternatively, you might attribute Charley’s success to a situational factor, such as an easy test; in that case, you make a situation attribution.
knowledge_points.plain: 把行为归因于情境因素

knowledge_points.name: Consistency
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Consistency refers to how similarly the individual acts in the same situation over time.
knowledge_points.plain: 同一情境中行为的一致程度

knowledge_points.name: Distinctiveness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Distinctiveness refers to how similar this situation is to other situations in which we have watched Charley.
knowledge_points.plain: 当前情境与其他情境的相似度

knowledge_points.name: Consensus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Consensus asks us to consider how others in the same situation have responded.
knowledge_points.plain: 看他人在同一情境中的反应

knowledge_points.name: Self-fulfilling prophecy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Even more interesting is the idea that the expectations we have of others can influence the way those others behave.
knowledge_points.plain: 期望促使他人按预期行事

knowledge_points.name: Fundamental attribution error
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When looking at the behavior of others, people tend to overestimate the importance of dispositional factors and underestimate the role of situational variables.
knowledge_points.plain: 解释他人时高估性格因素

knowledge_points.name: Actor-observer bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Whereas the fundamental attribution error focuses on how we explain others’ behavior, the actor-observer bias explains both the actor’s tendency to attribute behavior to situational factors and the observer’s tendency to attribute behavior to dispositional factors.
knowledge_points.plain: 自己归因情境他人归因性格

knowledge_points.name: False-consensus effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The tendency for people to overestimate the number of people who agree with them is called the false-consensus effect.
knowledge_points.plain: 高估他人与自己意见一致

knowledge_points.name: Self-serving bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Self-serving bias is the tendency to take more credit for good outcomes than for bad ones.
knowledge_points.plain: 好结果揽功坏结果推责

knowledge_points.name: Just-world phenomenon
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This belief in a just world, known simply as the just-world phenomenon or just-world bias, in which misfortunes befall people who deserve them, can be seen in the tendency to blame victims.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为人们遭遇都是应得的

knowledge_points.name: Attitude
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An attitude is a set of beliefs and feelings.
knowledge_points.plain: 对事物的信念与感受

knowledge_points.name: Mere exposure effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The mere exposure effect states that the more one is exposed to something, the more one will come to like it.
knowledge_points.plain: 接触越多越容易喜欢

knowledge_points.name: Elaboration likelihood model
knowledge_points.definition_quote: According to the elaboration likelihood model, persuasive messages can be processed through either the central route or the peripheral route.
knowledge_points.plain: 说服信息有两条加工路径

knowledge_points.name: Central route to persuasion
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The central route to persuasion involves deeply processing the content of the message
knowledge_points.plain: 深入加工信息内容来说服

knowledge_points.name: Peripheral route
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The peripheral route, on the other hand, involves other aspects of the message, including the characteristics of the person imparting the message (the communicator).
knowledge_points.plain: 靠信息之外线索来说服

knowledge_points.name: LaPiere study
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In 1934, Richard LaPiere conducted an early study that illustrated this difference (see Table 13.2).
knowledge_points.plain: 态度不能完全预测行为

knowledge_points.name: Cognitive dissonance theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Cognitive dissonance theory is based on the idea that people are motivated to have consistent attitudes and behaviors.
knowledge_points.plain: 态度行为不一致产生紧张

knowledge_points.name: Foot-in-the-door technique
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The foot- in-the-door technique suggests that if you can get people to agree to a small request, they will become more likely to agree to a follow-up request that is larger.
knowledge_points.plain: 先小请求后大请求

knowledge_points.name: Door-in-the-face technique
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The door-in-the-face technique argues that after people refuse a large request, they will look more favorably upon a follow- up request that seems, in comparison, much more reasonable.
knowledge_points.plain: 先大请求被拒再提小请求

knowledge_points.name: Norms of reciprocity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People tend to think that when someone does something nice for them, they ought to do something nice in return.
knowledge_points.plain: 受人恩惠应回报

knowledge_points.name: Social responsibility norm
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A related concept is the social responsibility norm, the belief that we all should do what we can to make the world and our society a better place.
knowledge_points.plain: 人人都应尽力改善社会

knowledge_points.name: Social trap
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A social trap is a situation in which the betterment of society requires us all to make some kind of sacrifice but our individual contribution is so small that people often choose to act in their own immediate interest instead of in the larger societal interest.
knowledge_points.plain: 个人私利导致集体受损

knowledge_points.name: Stereotypes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We all have ideas about what members of different groups are like, and these expectations may influence the way we interact with members of those groups. We call these ideas stereotypes.
knowledge_points.plain: 对某群体的概括看法

knowledge_points.name: Prejudice
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Prejudice is an undeserved, usually negative, attitude toward a group of people.
knowledge_points.plain: 对某群体不公正的负面态度

knowledge_points.name: Implicit attitude
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An explicit attitude is something someone is conscious of, while an implicit attitude is something that may influence someone’s behavior without their being aware of it.
knowledge_points.plain: 无意识影响行为的评价

knowledge_points.name: Ethnocentrism
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Ethnocentrism, the belief that one’s culture (e.g., ethnic, racial) is superior to others, is a specific kind of prejudice.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为自己文化优于其他文化

knowledge_points.name: Discrimination
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Prejudice is an attitude, but discrimination involves an action.
knowledge_points.plain: 基于偏见采取的行动

knowledge_points.name: Out-group homogeneity bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People tend to see members of their own group, the in-group, as more diverse than members of other groups, the out-groups. This phenomenon is often referred to as out-group homogeneity bias.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为外群体成员都相似

knowledge_points.name: In-group bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In addition, researchers have documented a preference for members of one’s own group, a kind of in-group bias.
knowledge_points.plain: 偏爱自己所属群体成员

knowledge_points.name: Categorization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some psychologists have suggested that people naturally and inevitably magnify differences between their own group and others as a function of the cognitive process of categorization.
knowledge_points.plain: 把人分类并夸大群体差异

knowledge_points.name: Contact theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The contact theory, as its name suggests, states that contact between hostile groups will reduce animosity but only if the groups are made to work toward a goal that benefits all and necessitates the participation of all.
knowledge_points.plain: 接触合作可减少敌意

knowledge_points.name: Superordinate goal
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The contact theory, as its name suggests, states that contact between hostile groups will reduce animosity but only if the groups are made to work toward a goal that benefits all and necessitates the participation of all. Such a goal is called a superordinate goal.
knowledge_points.plain: 需要群体共同合作的目标

knowledge_points.name: Instrumental aggression
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Instrumental aggression is when the aggressive act is intended to secure a particular end.
knowledge_points.plain: 为达到某种目的的攻击

knowledge_points.name: Hostile aggression
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Hostile aggression, on the other hand, has no such clear purpose.
knowledge_points.plain: 无明确目的的攻击

knowledge_points.name: Thanatos
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Freud linked aggression to Thanatos, the death instinct.
knowledge_points.plain: 弗洛伊德称攻击源于死本能

knowledge_points.name: Frustration-aggression hypothesis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One of the most influential theories, however, is known as the frustration-aggression hypothesis. This hypothesis holds that the feeling of frustration makes aggression more likely.
knowledge_points.plain: 挫折感增加攻击的可能性

knowledge_points.name: Bobo doll experiment
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another common theory is that the exposure to aggressive models makes people aggressive as illustrated by Bandura, Ross, and Ross’s (1963) classic Bobo doll experiment.
knowledge_points.plain: 观察攻击榜样会学得攻击

knowledge_points.name: Prosocial behavior
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Although social psychologists have devoted a lot of time and effort to studying antisocial behavior, they have also studied the factors that make people more likely to help one another. Such helping behavior is termed prosocial behavior.
knowledge_points.plain: 帮助他人的亲社会行为

knowledge_points.name: Bystander intervention
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Much of the research in this area has focused on bystander intervention, the conditions under which people nearby are more and are less likely to help someone in trouble.
knowledge_points.plain: 旁观者在什么条件下出手

knowledge_points.name: Bystander effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Counterintuitively, the larger the number of people who witness an emergency situation, the less likely any one is to intervene. This finding is known as the bystander effect.
knowledge_points.plain: 旁观者越多越少有人帮助

knowledge_points.name: Diffusion of responsibility
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One explanation for this phenomenon is called diffusion of responsibility. The larger the group of people who witness a problem, the less responsible any one individual feels to help.
knowledge_points.plain: 人越多个人责任感越弱

knowledge_points.name: Pluralistic ignorance
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another factor contributing to the bystander effect is known as pluralistic ignorance. People seem to decide what constitutes appropriate behavior in a situation by looking to others.
knowledge_points.plain: 靠观察他人判断该如何做

knowledge_points.name: Similarity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Although conventional wisdom holds that opposites attract, psychological research indicates that we are drawn to people who are similar to us, those who share our attitudes, backgrounds, and interests.
knowledge_points.plain: 人们喜欢与自己相似的人

knowledge_points.name: Proximity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Proximity means nearness.
knowledge_points.plain: 空间距离近容易产生吸引

knowledge_points.name: Reciprocal liking
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Thus, the more someone likes you, the more you will probably like that person.
knowledge_points.plain: 对方喜欢你你也更喜欢对方

knowledge_points.name: Self-disclosure
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One self-discloses when one shares a piece of personal information with another.
knowledge_points.plain: 分享个人私密信息

knowledge_points.name: Social facilitation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This phenomenon, that the presence of others improves task performance, is known as social facilitation.
knowledge_points.plain: 他人在场提高任务表现

knowledge_points.name: Social impairment
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Later studies, however, found that when the task being observed was a difficult one rather than a simple, well-practiced skill, being watched by others actually hurt performance, a finding known as social impairment.
knowledge_points.plain: 他人在场降低困难任务表现

knowledge_points.name: Upward social comparison
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Upward social comparison is when we compare ourselves to people doing better than we are, while downward social comparison is when we compare ourselves to people doing worse than we are.
knowledge_points.plain: 与比自己强的人比较

knowledge_points.name: Downward social comparison
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Upward social comparison is when we compare ourselves to people doing better than we are, while downward social comparison is when we compare ourselves to people doing worse than we are.
knowledge_points.plain: 与比自己差的人比较

knowledge_points.name: Relative deprivation theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Relative deprivation theory explains that people tend to feel less satisfied with their lives when they engage in a lot of upward social comparison.
knowledge_points.plain: 向上比较降低生活满意度

knowledge_points.name: Conformity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Conformity is the tendency of people to go along with the views or actions of others.
knowledge_points.plain: 顺从群体观点或行为

knowledge_points.name: Normative social influence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Normative social influence is when people conform for social reasons—to belong to the group.
knowledge_points.plain: 为了归属群体而顺从

knowledge_points.name: Informational social influence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: On the other hand, informational social influence leads to conformity because people think the group knows best.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为群体更懂而顺从

knowledge_points.name: Obedience
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Although conformity involves following a group without being explicitly told to do so, obedience studies have focused on participants’ willingness to do what another asks them to do.
knowledge_points.plain: 按权威要求行事的意愿

knowledge_points.name: Norms
knowledge_points.definition_quote: All groups have norms, which are rules about how group members should act.
knowledge_points.plain: 群体成员应如何行事的规则

knowledge_points.name: Social loafing
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Social loafing is the phenomenon when individuals do not put in as much effort when acting as part of a group as they do when acting alone.
knowledge_points.plain: 群体中个人努力减少

knowledge_points.name: Group polarization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Group polarization is the tendency of a group to make more extreme decisions than the group members would make individually.
knowledge_points.plain: 群体决策比个人更极端

knowledge_points.name: Groupthink
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Groupthink, a term coined by Irving Janis, describes the tendency for some groups to make bad decisions. Groupthink occurs when group members suppress their reservations about the ideas supported by the group.
knowledge_points.plain: 压制异议导致错误决策

knowledge_points.name: Deindividuation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This loss of self-restraint occurs when group members feel anonymous and aroused, and this phenomenon is known as deindividuation.
knowledge_points.plain: 匿名和兴奋下丧失自我约束

knowledge_points.name: Zimbardo’s prison experiment
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One famous experiment that showed not only how such conditions can cause people to deindividuate but also the effect of roles and the situation in general is Philip Zimbardo’s prison experiment (see Table 13.2).
knowledge_points.plain: 角色扮演使人变得残忍

knowledge_points.name: Personality
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychologists define personality as the unique attitudes, behaviors, and emotions that characterize a person.
knowledge_points.plain: 个人独特的典型态度行为情感

knowledge_points.name: Type A
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Type A people tend to feel a sense of time pressure and are easily angered.
knowledge_points.plain: 有时间紧迫感易怒的人

knowledge_points.name: Type B
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Type B individuals, on the other hand, tend to be relaxed and easygoing.
knowledge_points.plain: 放松随和的人

knowledge_points.name: Id
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The id is in the unconscious and contains instincts and psychic energy.
knowledge_points.plain: 本能与心理能量的来源

knowledge_points.name: Ego
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The ego follows the reality principle, which means its job is to negotiate between the desires of the id and the limitations of the environment.
knowledge_points.plain: 协调本我与现实环境

knowledge_points.name: Superego
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Around the age of five, children begin to develop a conscience and to think about what is right and wrong. This sense of conscience, according to Freud, is their superego.
knowledge_points.plain: 内化的良心与是非感

knowledge_points.name: Defense mechanisms
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The ego uses defense mechanisms to help protect the conscious mind.
knowledge_points.plain: 保护意识免受威胁的策略

knowledge_points.name: Repression
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Blocking thoughts out from conscious awareness.
knowledge_points.plain: 把想法挡在意识之外

knowledge_points.name: Denial
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Not accepting the ego-threatening truth.
knowledge_points.plain: 拒绝接受威胁性事实

knowledge_points.name: Displacement
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Redirecting one’s feelings toward another person or object.
knowledge_points.plain: 把情绪转移到他人或物

knowledge_points.name: Projection
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Believing that the feelings one has toward someone else are actually held by the other person and directed at oneself.
knowledge_points.plain: 把自己的感受归为他人所有

knowledge_points.name: Reaction Formation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Expressing the opposite of how one truly feels.
knowledge_points.plain: 表现出与真实感受相反

knowledge_points.name: Regression
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Returning to an earlier, comforting form of behavior.
knowledge_points.plain: 退回早期令人安心的行为

knowledge_points.name: Rationalization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Coming up with a beneficial result of an undesirable occurrence.
knowledge_points.plain: 为不好结果找出好处

knowledge_points.name: Intellectualization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Undertaking an academic, unemotional study of a topic.
knowledge_points.plain: 用学术方式冷静分析问题

knowledge_points.name: Sublimation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Channeling one’s frustration toward a different goal.
knowledge_points.plain: 把挫折转向其他目标

knowledge_points.name: Collective unconscious
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The collective unconscious is passed down through the species and, according to Jung, explains certain similarities we see among cultures.
knowledge_points.plain: 全人类共享的遗传潜意识

knowledge_points.name: Archetypes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The collective unconscious contains archetypes that Jung defined as universal concepts we all share as part of the human species.
knowledge_points.plain: 人类共有的普遍概念

knowledge_points.name: Inferiority
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Adler believed that people are motivated by the fear of failure, which he termed inferiority, and the desire to achieve, which he called superiority.
knowledge_points.plain: 害怕失败的自卑感

knowledge_points.name: Projective tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychodynamic theorists may use projective tests to try to delve into the unconscious. These tests involve asking people to interpret ambiguous stimuli.
knowledge_points.plain: 让受测者解释模糊刺激

knowledge_points.name: Rorschach inkblot test
knowledge_points.definition_quote: For instance, the Rorschach inkblot test involves showing people a series of inkblots and asking them to describe what they see.
knowledge_points.plain: 用墨迹图探测潜意识

knowledge_points.name: Thematic apperception test (TAT)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The thematic apperception test (TAT) consists of several cards, each of which contains a picture of a person or people in an ambiguous situation.
knowledge_points.plain: 用模糊图片编故事

knowledge_points.name: Determinism
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Determinism is the belief that what happens is dictated by what has happened in the past.
knowledge_points.plain: 过去决定现在与未来

knowledge_points.name: Free will
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Neither theory supports the existence of free will, which is an individual’s ability to choose his or her own destiny.
knowledge_points.plain: 个人选择自己命运的能力

knowledge_points.name: Third force
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This perspective is often referred to as the third force because it arose in opposition to the determinism so central to both psychoanalytic and behaviorist models.
knowledge_points.plain: 人本主义被称为第三势力

knowledge_points.name: Self-concept
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Self-concept is a person’s global feeling about himself or herself.
knowledge_points.plain: 对自己整体的看法和感受

knowledge_points.name: Self-actualization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: He believed that people are motivated to reach their full potential or self- actualize.
knowledge_points.plain: 发挥潜能实现自我

knowledge_points.name: Unconditional positive regard
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Unconditional positive regard is a kind of blanket acceptance.
knowledge_points.plain: 无条件的完全接纳

knowledge_points.name: Traits
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Trait theorists believe that we can describe people’s personalities by specifying their main characteristics, or traits.
knowledge_points.plain: 描述人格的稳定特征

knowledge_points.name: Nomothetic approach
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some trait theorists believe that the same basic set of traits can be used to describe all people’s personalities. Such a belief characterizes a nomothetic approach.
knowledge_points.plain: 用同一套特质描述所有人

knowledge_points.name: 16 PF
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Raymond Cattell developed the 16 PF (personality factor) test to measure what he believed were the 16 basic traits present in all people, albeit to different degrees.
knowledge_points.plain: 卡特尔16种人格因素测验

knowledge_points.name: Big Five personality traits
knowledge_points.definition_quote: More recently, Paul Costa and Robert McCrae have proposed that personality can be described using the Big Five personality traits: extroversion, agreeableness, conscientiousness, openness to experience, and emotional stability (or neuroticism).
knowledge_points.plain: 用五个维度描述人格

knowledge_points.name: Factor analysis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Factor analysis allows researchers to use correlations among traits to see which traits cluster together as factors.
knowledge_points.plain: 用相关找出特质群集

knowledge_points.name: Idiographic theorists
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Other trait theorists, called idiographic theorists, assert that using the same set of terms to classify all people is impossible.
knowledge_points.plain: 主张逐一研究个体独特性

knowledge_points.name: Cardinal dispositions
knowledge_points.definition_quote: He suggested that a small number of people are so profoundly influenced by one trait that it plays a pivotal role in virtually everything they do. He referred to such traits as cardinal dispositions.
knowledge_points.plain: 主导个体一切行为的特质

knowledge_points.name: Central dispositions
knowledge_points.definition_quote: As their names indicate, central dispositions have a larger influence on personality than secondary dispositions.
knowledge_points.plain: 影响较大的人格特质

knowledge_points.name: Reciprocal determinism
knowledge_points.definition_quote: His model is based on the idea of reciprocal determinism, also known as triadic reciprocality. These terms essentially mean that each of these three factors influences both of the other two in a constant, looplike fashion.
knowledge_points.plain: 人环境行为三者相互影响

knowledge_points.name: Self-efficacy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People with high self-efficacy are optimistic about their own ability to get things done, whereas people with low self-efficacy feel a sense of powerlessness.
knowledge_points.plain: 对自己完成任务的信心

knowledge_points.name: Locus of control
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A person can be described as having either an internal or an external locus of control.
knowledge_points.plain: 人对自己命运的控制感

knowledge_points.name: Internal locus of control
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People with an internal locus of control feel as if they are responsible for what happens to them.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为自己掌控命运

knowledge_points.name: External locus of control
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Conversely, people with an external locus of control generally believe that luck and other forces outside of their own control determine their destinies.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为运气等外部力量决定命运

knowledge_points.name: Explanatory style
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We can also differentiate people by their explanatory style—the kind of attributions they make about the things that happen to them.
knowledge_points.plain: 对事件的归因习惯

knowledge_points.name: Optimistic explanatory style
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some people have an optimistic explanatory style, which leads them to make internal, global, and stable attributions for good things that happen to them and external, specific, and unstable attributions for bad experiences.
knowledge_points.plain: 好事归己坏事归外因

knowledge_points.name: Personality inventories
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Personality inventories are essentially questionnaires that ask people to provide information about themselves.
knowledge_points.plain: 让人自我报告的问卷

knowledge_points.name: MMPI-2
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory (MMPI-2) is one of the most widely used self-report instruments.
knowledge_points.plain: 常用自评人格量表

knowledge_points.name: Barnum effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Research has demonstrated that people have the tendency to see themselves in vague, stock descriptions of personality.
knowledge_points.plain: 相信笼统描述适合自己

knowledge_points.name: Motivation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Motivations are feelings or ideas that cause us to act toward a goal.
knowledge_points.plain: 推动人朝目标行动的力量

knowledge_points.name: Instincts
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If you have pets, you know that different animals are born with instincts, which are automatic behaviors performed in response to specific stimuli.
knowledge_points.plain: 天生对特定刺激的反应

knowledge_points.name: Drive reduction theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One early theory about how our physiology motivates us was drive reduction theory, the theory that our behavior is motivated by biological needs.
knowledge_points.plain: 行为由生理需要驱动

knowledge_points.name: Need
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A need is one of our requirements for survival, such as food, water, or shelter.
knowledge_points.plain: 生存所必需的条件

knowledge_points.name: Drive
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A drive is our impulse to act in a way that satisfies this need.
knowledge_points.plain: 满足需要的内在冲动

knowledge_points.name: Homeostasis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our body seeks homeostasis, which is a balanced internal state.
knowledge_points.plain: 身体追求的内部平衡状态

knowledge_points.name: Primary drives
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Primary drives are biological needs, like thirst.
knowledge_points.plain: 与生俱来的生理需要

knowledge_points.name: Secondary drives
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Secondary drives are learned drives.
knowledge_points.plain: 后天习得的驱力

knowledge_points.name: Arousal theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some motivations that seem to violate biological theories of motivation can be explained by arousal theory (or sensation- seeking theory), which states that we seek an optimum level of excitement or arousal.
knowledge_points.plain: 追求最佳唤醒水平

knowledge_points.name: Yerkes-Dodson law
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In general, most of us perform best with an optimal level of arousal, although this varies with different activities. We might perform well at an easy task with a very high level of arousal, but the same high level of arousal would prevent us from performing well on a difficult task.
knowledge_points.plain: 任务难度与最佳唤醒水平的关系

knowledge_points.name: Opponent-process theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, the theory states that we eventually feel an opponent process, meaning a motivation to return to our baseline, neutral state.
knowledge_points.plain: 偏离基线后产生反向动机

knowledge_points.name: Incentives
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Incentives are stimuli that we are drawn to due to learning.
knowledge_points.plain: 后天习得的有吸引力刺激

knowledge_points.name: Self-determination theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Self-determination research indicates that three elements are related to intrinsic motivations involved in what they call self- determination: autonomy, competence, and relatedness.
knowledge_points.plain: 内在动机基于三种需要

knowledge_points.name: Autonomy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Autonomy is the belief that we have the power to make choices that are important to us.
knowledge_points.plain: 相信自己能自主选择

knowledge_points.name: Competence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Competence is the belief that we have the skills and knowledge needed to accomplish tasks important to us.
knowledge_points.plain: 相信自己具备完成任务的能力

knowledge_points.name: Relatedness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Relatedness is our ability to form relationships with others who are important to us.
knowledge_points.plain: 与他人建立重要关系

knowledge_points.name: Hypothalamus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The hypothalamus monitors and helps to control body chemistry (including the ratio of glucose and insulin) and makes us feel hungry when we need to eat.
knowledge_points.plain: 调节身体化学并产生饥饿感

knowledge_points.name: Lateral hypothalamus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The lateral hypothalamus (hunger center), when stimulated, causes the animal to eat.
knowledge_points.plain: 刺激时促使进食的饥饿中枢

knowledge_points.name: Ventromedial hypothalamus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another part of the hypothalamus, the ventromedial hypothalamus (satiety center), causes the animal to stop eating when it is stimulated.
knowledge_points.plain: 刺激时停止进食的饱食中枢

knowledge_points.name: Ghrelin
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Ghrelin influences short-term hunger; it’s produced in the stomach and communicates hunger to the brain.
knowledge_points.plain: 胃分泌的短期饥饿激素

knowledge_points.name: Leptin
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Leptin is produced by fat cells and signals the brain that you have sufficient stored energy and thus are not hungry.
knowledge_points.plain: 脂肪细胞分泌的饱腹信号

knowledge_points.name: Set-point theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Set-point theory describes how the hypothalamus might decide what impulse to send. This theory states that the hypothalamus wants to maintain a certain optimum body weight.
knowledge_points.plain: 下丘脑维持理想体重设定点

knowledge_points.name: Externals
knowledge_points.definition_quote: For example, research indicates that some of us (called externals) are more motivated to eat by external food cues, such as attractiveness or availability of food.
knowledge_points.plain: 易受外部食物线索影响者

knowledge_points.name: Internals
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Others (called internals) are less affected by the presence and presentation of food and respond more often to internal hunger cues.
knowledge_points.plain: 更依内部饥饿信号进食者

knowledge_points.name: Garcia effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This is caused by the Garcia effect and occurs whenever nausea is paired with either food or drink.
knowledge_points.plain: 恶心与食物配对形成厌恶

knowledge_points.name: Bulimia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People with bulimia eat large amounts of food in a short period of time (binging) and then get rid of the food (purging) by vomiting, exercising excessively, or using laxatives.
knowledge_points.plain: 暴食后催吐或清除食物

knowledge_points.name: Anorexia nervosa
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People with anorexia starve themselves to below 85 percent of their normal body weight and refuse to eat due to their obsession with weight.
knowledge_points.plain: 因执着体重而极度节食

knowledge_points.name: Sexual response cycle
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The famous lab studies done by William Masters and Virginia Johnson documented the sexual response cycle in men and women.
knowledge_points.plain: 性反应经历四个阶段

knowledge_points.name: Refractory period
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Male systems experience a refractory period—a time period that must elapse before another orgasm.
knowledge_points.plain: 男性再次高潮前的恢复期

knowledge_points.name: Sexual desire
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Sexual desire can be present even when the capability to have sex is lost.
knowledge_points.plain: 性能力丧失后仍有性欲

knowledge_points.name: Kinsey Reports
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Researchers (like Alfred Kinsey, who documented the variety of human sexual behaviors in the famous Kinsey Reports from the 1940s and 1950s) have been able to dispel some common myths about sexuality.
knowledge_points.plain: 金赛报告记录性行为多样性

knowledge_points.name: Sexual orientation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Studies show that gay and lesbian sexual orientation is not related to traumatic childhood experiences, parenting styles, the quality of relationships with parents, masculinity or femininity, or the sexual orientation of our parents.
knowledge_points.plain: 性取向与养育方式无关

knowledge_points.name: Achievement motivation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Achievement motivation examines our desires to master complex tasks and knowledge and to reach personal goals.
knowledge_points.plain: 掌握任务与达成目标的动机

knowledge_points.name: Extrinsic motivations
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Extrinsic motivations are rewards that we get for accomplishments from outside ourselves (for example, grades, salary, and so on).
knowledge_points.plain: 来自外部的奖励

knowledge_points.name: Intrinsic motivations
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Intrinsic motivations are rewards we get internally, such as enjoyment or satisfaction.
knowledge_points.plain: 来自内部的满足感

knowledge_points.name: Theory X
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Theory X Managers believe that employees will work only if rewarded with benefits or threatened with punishment.
knowledge_points.plain: 管理者认为员工只为奖惩工作

knowledge_points.name: Theory Y
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Theory Y Managers believe that employees are internally motivated to do good work and policies should encourage this internal motive.
knowledge_points.plain: 管理者相信员工内在动机

knowledge_points.name: Approach-approach conflict
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The first, named an approach-approach conflict, occurs when you must choose between two desirable outcomes.
knowledge_points.plain: 在两个都想得到的目标间选择

knowledge_points.name: Avoidance-avoidance conflict
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another type of conflict, an avoidance-avoidance conflict, occurs when you must choose between two unattractive outcomes.
knowledge_points.plain: 在两个都不想要的目标间选择

knowledge_points.name: Approach-avoidance conflict
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An approach-avoidance conflict exists when one event or goal has both attractive and unattractive features.
knowledge_points.plain: 同一目标既有吸引力又令人排斥

knowledge_points.name: Multiple approach-avoidance conflicts
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Finally, people experience multiple approach-avoidance conflicts. In these, you must choose between two or more things, each of which has both desirable and undesirable features.
knowledge_points.plain: 多个各有利弊的选项间选择

knowledge_points.name: James-Lange theory
knowledge_points.subheading: What Comes First—The Emotion or the Physiological Change?
knowledge_points.definition_quote: They theorized that we feel emotion because of biological changes caused by stress.
knowledge_points.plain: 生理变化在先情绪在后

knowledge_points.name: Facial feedback hypothesis
knowledge_points.subheading: What Comes First—The Emotion or the Physiological Change?
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The facial feedback hypothesis is a related idea that suggests that we infer our emotions from our facial expressions.
knowledge_points.plain: 根据面部表情推断情绪

knowledge_points.name: Cannon-Bard theory
knowledge_points.subheading: What Comes First—The Emotion or the Physiological Change?
knowledge_points.definition_quote: They theorized that the biological change and the cognitive awareness of the emotional state occur simultaneously.
knowledge_points.plain: 生理变化与情绪认知同时发生

knowledge_points.name: Two-factor theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Schachter pointed out that both our physical responses and our cognitive appraisal of them (our mental interpretations) combine to cause any particular emotional response.
knowledge_points.plain: 生理唤醒加认知标签形成情绪

knowledge_points.name: Broaden-and-build theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another theory of emotion known as the broaden-and-build theory focuses specifically on the power and potential of positive emotions. This theory contends that positive emotions facilitate a playful and experimental mindset, which makes it easier for people to expand their social interactions and try new activities.
knowledge_points.plain: 积极情绪拓展思维与行动

knowledge_points.name: Facial expressions
knowledge_points.definition_quote: No matter what culture we grew up in, we are likely to use the same facial expressions for basic emotions like happiness, sadness, anger, disgust, surprise, and fear.
knowledge_points.plain: 基本情绪的面部表情跨文化一致

knowledge_points.name: Sociobiology
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This area of research (sometimes called sociobiology) indicates that the facial expressions we make for basic emotions may be an innate part of our physiological makeup.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究表情的先天生理基础

knowledge_points.name: Display rules
knowledge_points.definition_quote: On the other hand, researchers have documented some differences in how people express emotion. One cause is thought to be different cultural display rules.
knowledge_points.plain: 文化规定情绪表达方式
